lead: six minutes in a queue, a stranger's third sentence, and you had him — what he was avoiding, what he would be good at. he left with a name to ring. he never got yours.
sun: the read arrives inside a minute and your hands have somewhere to put it before the conversation is over. so a stranger gets the introduction, the sentence, the name of the person who does that work — sized to what you saw rather than to what they asked for. it is accurate, it works, and it goes out carrying nothing that would let anyone trace where the accuracy came from.
moon: and then the contact does not release. the push left in ninety seconds and the man did not: he is filed whole — the pause before he answered, the job he had already decided to lose — and he stays at that resolution for twenty years, a person you are carrying who has no memory of your face. the giving is instant. the holding has no mechanism for ending.
pull: you hand a stranger their next ten years in the length of a queue. they leave with the working half. you keep the person, entire, at the resolution of that afternoon.
tension: strangers find you easy to talk to and impossible to place. nothing about you can be read from across a room — what you have done is in other households, under other people's names — so a first impression settles on manner alone, and manner is the only material anyone has ever had of you. intense is the usual verdict, or too much too early, delivered by people you had already read correctly before they sat down.
cost: a stranger's real difficulty, named and acted on before the coffee arrives, cannot be bought anywhere, and hundreds have gone off with the result. the read behind it never travels. it stays at full grain for decades and so does the person, so your side of those meetings is an archive nobody has been shown and nobody can be handed.

lead: when you go, the speech will be about the seat and how steadily it was held. four of the things this place runs on came out of your hands. none of those will be mentioned.
sun: you have started things from inside a structure, which is the one place a start is guaranteed to lose its author. the practice you began in somebody's office is now policy; the unit is on the chart; the way the intake is done is the way it has always been done. an institution absorbs by design, and your hands make the one kind of thing it absorbs completely.
moon: the seat was carved before you got near it, and the bearing that comes with it does not permit a claim: someone who lists what they started, from a chair, is describing exactly the unease the chair exists to have settled. so the one file that would answer your own question about whether you belong here is the file you are structurally unable to submit.
pull: the room believes you inherited well. what it runs on, you started, and every start of yours has belonged to the institution since about the second week.
tension: the word is custodian, meant kindly, by people who mean steady and unbroken. succession is where it bites: you will hand on a position you did not build, having built most of what stands under it, and there is a procedure for the first of those and none at all for the second. the colleagues who could confirm any of it are the ones whose names the work went out under.
cost: things you put into an institution survive you by decades, because they enter wearing its clothes — no champion needed, nobody attached to them for a successor to resent. the place is genuinely better and the improvement has no author. you are left holding a standing that arrived with the chair, and a private account of what you did that would sound, said aloud, like arguing with your own obituary.

lead: people describe you to other people as someone who gets things going. asked for an example, they pause, and then they describe you a second time, with more feeling and no instance in it.
sun: at this width the material comes to you unsolicited. three people in an evening will set a half-formed thing down where you can reach it, and your hands take it up before anyone has decided anything — the shape found, the first move named, the person to call produced from nowhere. by the following week it is theirs, running, and it was theirs from the hour it first worked.
moon: what you are reads from the far end of a room, at a scale nobody chose and nothing can lower, so people arrive at you already mid-sentence. nothing precedes the asking — no letter, no favour called in, no moment where someone has to name what they want and be seen wanting it. the start of each of these is a conversation neither party would afterwards call a request.
pull: you are known for a size, and known widely. what the size has actually produced is running in nine other lives, and nobody once had to ask you for it.
tension: you are discussed, at length, by people who have never watched you do anything. when one of them finally asks what you have built, every honest answer is a story about somebody who then went off and did something, which sounds out loud like claiming other people's lives as your work. so the estimate holds, and holds high, and nothing under it can be inspected.
cost: more gets set going through you in a year than most people start in a lifetime, at a rate only this much visibility can supply. none of it deposits. the width brings in more of the same traffic, and the traffic is the entire record — a large impression, held by hundreds, of work they could not describe if asked.

lead: the trade ended in one season, absolutely, the way endings arrive in you. nothing you started in those twenty years so much as slowed. there was no one it was necessary to tell.
sun: an ending here has nothing to dispose of. what you made was already elsewhere — passed on at the second handoff, absorbed, renamed, running on other people's hours — so when you finished there was no equipment to sell, no client to place, no successor to brief. the closing year a maker usually gets was not available to you. the whole of it took a fortnight.
moon: the season closed over the whole of that person: the appetite, the reasons, the name people used then. what the turn cannot lift off is the owing, and here that is the entire residue — no objects, no premises, no craft carried over, only the people you still answer to, out of a life you can no longer describe from inside.
pull: the ending was absolute and it did not reach one thing you made. all of it is still running, elsewhere, on schedule, and none of it required telling.
tension: nobody can see that anything ended. an ending shows in its wake — the vacancy, the stalled work, the people at a loss — and yours produced none, because nothing was attached firmly enough to register a departure. so the leaving gets read as restlessness, and the ones who liked you say you could have stayed. what would answer them is twenty years of output, dispersed, doing fine without you.
cost: you can close a life at the root and harm nobody, because nothing in it was running on your continued presence — every piece of it was self-supporting from its first month, by construction. the account stays in the town. what crossed the line with you is a short list of duties, and what those twenty years amounted to sits in pieces with people you will not see again.
